title: HIV and development

blocks.heading: HIV and development
blocks.text: HIV-related illness can affect work, household care and public resources in Namibia and other SADC economies, while effective care improves opportunities to remain well and participate. Accessible testing, treatment and support form part of a public-health response. Avoid treating HIV status as incapacity or using a fictional illness series as actual national prevalence evidence.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Economic pathways
blocks.text: Illness or premature death can reduce available labour, increase caring work and divert household resources. Treatment access and support can reduce these burdens; stigma and exclusion can add avoidable economic costs independently of health status.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: System responses
blocks.text: HIV responses can combine prevention information, confidential testing, ongoing treatment, maternal-child services and community support. Continuity, trained services and non-stigmatising access matter. Individual treatment decisions belong with qualified health professionals, not a classroom model answer.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Follow the mechanism
blocks.text: Explain the economic pathway in an invented household where illness interrupts paid work and another member reduces hours to provide care, while savings are limited. Lost paid hours reduce income while care limits a second earner’s time. Limited savings make the combined loss harder to absorb; continued health and social support could address the burden without excluding affected people.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Use accurate HIV language
blocks.text: [WHO’s HIV fact sheet](https://www.who.int/en/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/hiv-aids), checked 20 October 2026, explains that treatment can control HIV and that ordinary contact such as sharing food does not transmit it. Do not use a diagnosis as a reason to exclude someone from schooling or work. This lesson does not prescribe individual treatment.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect to Population (7.1), Development (1.1) and Education (7.3). Separate installed facilities, usable coverage and health outcomes. Synthetic figures model reasoning and are not current Namibian statistics.
